report:
### Conclusion
**Yes**, the additional offer of HIV self-testing (HIVST) causes more people to take an HIV test compared to standard testing services alone.

### Evidence
Systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) consistently show that offering HIV self-testing increases testing reach and frequency:

* **Overall Uptake and Frequency:** Meta-analyses of RCTs comparing HIVST to standard testing services show that self-testing significantly increases both testing uptake and frequency, particularly among individuals at risk who might otherwise avoid clinic-based testing (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.7448/IAS.20.1.21594, https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0245498).
* **Key Populations:** A systematic review of RCTs found that HIVST increases testing uptake and frequency among key groups, such as men who have sex with men and transgender individuals (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12916-020-01835-z).
* **Prevention Scale-Up:** Clinical trial evidence shows that introducing self-testing options substantially enhances testing uptake across various HIV prevention strategies (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanhiv/article/PIIS2352-3018(24)00187-5/fulltext).
